title: The frontend offers 78 UK ports and airports as the port of exit; DR1 offers only the ten border control posts approved for animals, so a user can choose a port their consignment cannot lawfully leave from.

finding.frontend: Port of exit is a select of 78 entries drawn from the general ports-of-entry reference list — Aberdeen Harbour, Cambridge Airport, Chatham Docks and the rest — each labelled with a UN location code, and the hint says so: 'Choose where the consignment will leave Great Britain. Exit and entry share the same port list.' Nothing marks which of them can handle animals, and any of the 78 is accepted (src/server/app/services/ports/index.js:9-14, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/port-of-exit/copy/copy.en.js:5-6).
finding.prototype: DR1 offers ten, and every one of them is a border control post designated for live animals, labelled with its BCP code: Edinburgh, Gatwick, Glasgow, three Heathrow posts, Holyhead, Manchester, Prestwick and Stansted (app/data/exit-border-control-posts.js:3-14). Anything else is rejected with 'Select a port of exit'. The same ten serve both the transit reveal and the temporary-admission reveal — DR1 uses one exit list, not one list per reason.
finding.difference: Restrict the port of exit to ports designated for live animals and label each with its BCP code, so the user cannot pick a port that cannot receive the consignment. The frontend does not hold that designation: the ports list it reads carries a code and a name and nothing else, so this needs the reference data service either to expose the designation or to serve an animal-BCP list of its own. Until that lands the frontend cannot filter. Drop the 'Exit and entry share the same port list' hint at the same time — DR1's exit list is not the entry list, so the sentence would be wrong.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a DR1 port-of-exit select offering a port that is not an animal border control post, or finding that the ten-entry list is applied only under a design-release-2 branch.
finding.correction: Both counts re-derived and correct, and the needs-backend band holds. COUNTS: the frontend's captured port-of-exit select carries 80 options — a 'Select port of exit' placeholder, a disabled divider and 78 ports — counted from capture/html/frontend/fe-port-of-exit.html, and the entries do read as the general list ('Aberdeen Airport (GB DYC)', 'Aberdeen Harbour (GB ABD)', 'Avonmouth Docks (GB AVO)' and so on). DR1's two captured port selects each carry 11 options — a 'Select one' placeholder and 10 posts — matching app/data/exit-border-control-posts.js entry for entry, and the two selects hold the identical ten, so the finding is right that DR1 uses one exit list rather than one per reason. Nothing in the DR1 ten appears in the frontend's 78: 'Heathrow Airport – Airpets Limited (animals)' and its siblings have no counterpart in the ports-of-entry data, so this is a different list, not a subset. BAND ARGUED AND CORRECT: the frontend's ports come from the reference data service (fetchPortsOfEntry against /ports-of-entry, src/server/app/services/ports/client.js) and every record is exactly { code, name } — verified against the captured fixture at src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json. There is no designation field to filter on, so needs-backend is right and the finding is not schedulable as frontend-only work. ONE THING THE PICKER MUST KNOW, not a defect in this finding: the frontend's behaviour is not an accident. The V4 requirement recorded against the portOfExit obligation states the opposite of DR1 — 'Port selected from the port of entry list (Exit and Entry share the same list)' (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js) — which is where the hint sentence comes from. DR1 is the signed-off definition and so wins, but the two sources genuinely conflict and someone should close that rather than assume the frontend simply missed the rule. HOW CHECKED: counted option elements in both captured DOMs; compared the two lists entry by entry; read the ports service, its client and its fixture; read the port-of-exit copy file and the portOfExit obligation.
